correctness.rationale: For a one-pole characteristic-seven Artin–Schreier cover of genus nine, Riemann–Hurwitz forces reduced pole degree four. Valuations -7,-4 and different exponent 30 yield an exact nine-form basis with weight inequality 7i+4j<=16. The Cartier formula from y^7=y+f selects only x exponents 6 mod 7. Direct polynomial expansion in F_7[a,b] verifies all 81 entries, with 8 nonzero symbolic entries. The displayed matrix has ranks 3 for a!=0, 2 for a=0,b!=0, and 0 for a=b=0; the a-numbers are 9 minus rank, hence 6,7,9. Symbolic identities cover algebraically closed parameter fields; the program was run and returned VERIFY_OK.

originality.rationale: The closest primary literature constructs a minimal automorphism example and settles the genus/p-rank range without computing a-number strata. Earlier characteristic-divisibility a-number formulas do not apply to jump 4 at p=7; known monomial a-number formulas already imply the special origin value, which is not separately claimed as new. General Artin–Schreier cover bounds do not supply an exhaustive 3-stratum classification. The accepted claim is the full classification and forbidden a-number 8, not any known monomial example.

value.rationale: A natural complete stratum—not an arbitrary isolated example—is classified: every characteristic-seven genus-nine p-rank-zero Artin–Schreier curve has a-number exactly 6,7, or9. Two exact jumping loci and forbidden value8 are determined by a single transparent symbolic matrix. It refines the recently identified minimal-automorphism genus-nine cover, distinguishes Jacobian invariants invisible to genus and p-rank, and supplies a precise test case for deformation and Ekedahl–Oort stratifications without overstating those as proved.
